_readme: OPTIONAL. You only need an entry here if a photograph needs fixing.
Most people never touch this file — drop images in source/ and run
`npm run images` and that is the whole job.
Key = the filename as it sits in source/ (just the name, not the folder).
crop:   { left, top, width, height }  in pixels on the original,
measured AFTER any sideways-phone rotation is corrected.
Use this to cut burned-in text off an edge. Crop inward from the
edge holding the text; never blur or clone it out.
rotate: degrees clockwise, for levelling a horizon that is a degree off.
ignoreExifOrientation: true — for a file stored the right way round that
still carries a rotation tag from an earlier edit. Symptom: the
photograph appears on its side on the site but looks fine in
Preview. `npm run check` flags any file carrying such a tag.
slug:   the filename used on the website. Defaults to the filename.
note:   free text, echoed into rejects.txt.
Originals in source/ are never modified. Everything happens here so a crop
can be reviewed, changed and undone.

_settings._note: targetLongEdge is the widest any photograph is ever stored at. Nothing on the site is displayed above about 1300 CSS pixels, so 1600 covers a 2x screen at the widest slot. Raising it will blow the 400KB-per-image budget that npm run build enforces.
